questions.stem: The three main components of the cardiovascular system are:
options: The heart
The lungs
The blood vessels
The blood
questions.explanation: Heart, blood vessels and blood, working together.

options: Delivers oxygen, nutrients and hormones
Removes carbon dioxide and other waste products
Is also called the circulatory system
Produces bile
questions.explanation: Bile is produced by the liver.

questions.stem: About the chambers of the heart:
options: The two atria are at the top
There are four chambers
The two ventricles are at the bottom
The ventricles are the upper chambers
questions.explanation: Atria = upper chambers; ventricles = lower pumping chambers.

questions.stem: The right side of the heart:
options: Propels oxygenated blood into the systemic circulation
Pumps blood to the lungs
Has no ventricle
Pumps blood directly to the brain
questions.explanation: The left side propels oxygenated blood into the systemic circulation.

questions.stem: The strict separation between the right and left sides of the heart is important because:
options: It prevents oxygen-rich and oxygen-poor blood from mixing
It slows the heart rate
It allows blood to skip the lungs
It ensures efficiency
questions.explanation: "The strict division… ensures efficiency by preventing oxygen-rich and oxygen-poor blood from mixing."

questions.stem: Match the blood vessel to its function:
options: Capillaries — fine exchange sites with cells
Arteries — carry blood away from the heart under strong pressure
Veins — carry blood away from the heart under strong pressure
Veins — return blood to the heart with the help of valves
questions.explanation: Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins bring it back.

questions.stem: Match the blood component to its role:
options: Red blood cells — contain hemoglobin to transport oxygen
Plasma — carries hemoglobin inside white cells
White blood cells — defend the body against pathogens
Platelets — contribute to clot formation
questions.explanation: Hemoglobin is in red blood cells.

questions.stem: Blood is described in the text as:
options: A muscular organ
A nervous tissue
A specialized connective tissue
A type of epithelium
questions.explanation: "The blood itself is a specialized connective tissue."

options: Is entirely voluntary
Is achieved through neural and hormonal control
Adrenaline prepares the system for stress or physical effort
The autonomic nervous system adjusts heart rate and vessel diameter
questions.explanation: The autonomic nervous system controls involuntary functions.

questions.stem: Besides circulating blood, the cardiovascular system participates in:
options: Immune defence
Temperature regulation
Producing hormones such as insulin
Coordination of complex physiological processes
questions.explanation: The text lists temperature regulation, immune defence and coordination of processes.

questions.stem: Match each term to its definition:
options: Capillary — the smallest blood vessel, where exchange with tissues occurs
Ventricle — a small blood component that helps clotting
Atrium — one of the upper chambers of the heart
Hemoglobin — the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen
questions.explanation: Ventricle = one of the lower pumping chambers; platelet = clotting component.

questions.stem: The correct passive form of "Red blood cells transport oxygen" is:
options: Oxygen transported red blood cells.
Red blood cells are transported by oxygen.
Oxygen is transported by red blood cells.
Oxygen is transporting by red blood cells.
questions.explanation: Object → subject + is + past participle + by agent.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct passive forms?
options: Blood is pumped to the lungs by the heart.
The body is defended against pathogens by white blood cells.
The heart rate is adjusted by the autonomic nervous system.
Oxygen is absorb in the lungs.
questions.explanation: The passive needs the past participle: "is absorbed".

options: The agent can be introduced with "by"
The verb is formed with be + past participle
The object of the active sentence becomes the subject
The verb is always in the -ing form
questions.explanation: e.g. "Oxygen is absorbed in the lungs and is then transported to tissues by red blood cells."
